messages.author: 5833f786297b5efd
messages.subject: [Shiny-server] Directory index and file download
parts:
Hi,

My question is related to shiny-server, and not to shiny :
I'm using a server (with shiny-server running on it) to publish shiny apps.

Until my last update of shiny-server (now running Shiny Server v1.2.1.362 ), I also used this server to host html websites, and to serve some files (pdf etc.)

Since this update, the HTML hosting still works, but it's not possible anymore for users to download files : the server returns a "Not found" error.

  • So, my first question is : how can I configure shiny-server so that it allows to download files ?

Another side effect of this update is that now, Rmd files are compiled/rendered by shiny-server.
I used to let my users download Rmd files of my projects, so that they can access the source of it. Now, when they open the Rmd, it's rendered as HTML, so, they can't get the source.
  • Is there a way, on a specific directory, to tell shiny-server not to interpret the RMarkdown ?

My last question is also related to the first ones. Is it possible, as would a basic nginx do, to display the content of a directory ? using directory_index on allows to show the directories, but I would also like to display (and be able for the user to download...) the files contained in a directory.

  • Is it possible to setup shiny-server to display the content (files and folder) of a folder ? Like nginx does with autoindex on ?


Thanks for your help,


Robin

Robin Cura
Doctorant à l'UMR Géographie-cités
LabEx DynamiTe & Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: [Shiny-server] Directory index and file download
parts:
Hi Robin,

I think these are all a result of Shiny Server's support for Rmd file. As you said, Shiny Server is now compiling/rendering Rmd files as HTML. I don't think there is a workaround for this at the moment, but we will look into this issue.

But the other 2 issues you are seeing are side effects that you can work around them. If you have a directory that does not contain Shiny application files, there are 3 things that could happen:

1- No Rmd files => The files and directories are listed as you expect
2- index.Rmd exists => This file gets processed, and you would just see this instead of the directory listing
3- An Rmd file exists but it is not called index.Rmd (e.g. test.Rmd)  => This is the case that you see File Not Found.

So the workaround for the last 2 cases would be to separate your Rmd files from other files that you want to see as directory listing. 

Sorry for the inconvenience. We will look into providing a better solution for these.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.author: 077520bb1c6c7220
messages.subject: Re: [Shiny-server] Directory index and file download
parts:
Hi Fereshteh,

I'm experiencing the exact same issues as described by Robin. 
I have PDF files stored on my shiny server at /etc/svr/shiny-server/AppFolder/www/file.pdf and my app's Rmd file is located in /etc/svr/shiny-server/AppFolder. I am trying to display a link within the Rmarkdown document in a DT table for users to click and view the PDF. 
My DT table contains a column with the following string : <a href='http://server_name:3838/AppFolder/www/file.pdf' target='_blank' >MyFile</a>.  
I am able to render a link however , when clicking, I get a "Not found" page. Is there a workaround to enable opening the PDF files from the app ?
Many thanks for your help

Samy
